questions.q: What do the authors say about emotions at work?
a: They are always present and can be an asset
They should be hidden to stay professional
They only matter in your personal life
They disappear once you focus on tasks
questions.why: The overview argues emotions cannot be switched off and actually help us connect and empathize.

questions.q: What did Google's study find about the best teams?
a: They had high psychological safety
They had the most experienced managers
They had the largest budgets
They had the fewest meetings
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Google found psychological safety was the biggest factor in team performance.

questions.q: What does the summary say about strong emotions and decisions?
a: They can help us make better decisions
They always distort our judgment
They matter only for artists
They should be ignored at work
questions.why: Lesson 2 says strong emotions, good or bad, can help investors make better decisions.

questions.q: Which feelings does the summary call irrelevant and worth letting go?
a: A migraine or boredom in a meeting
Regret about accepting a new task
Happiness about finishing a project
Excitement about a possible raise
questions.why: Lesson 2 separates relevant emotions, which carry information, from irrelevant ones like a migraine or meeting boredom.

questions.q: What does the summary say about skipping paid time off?
a: It leads to burnout and lower motivation
It is expected of committed employees
It should be saved for emergencies
It makes teams more productive
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Americans rarely take paid leave, which fuels demotivation and burnout.
